media.alt: Cricket match inaugurates first phase of AKU sports centre

content.text: "To mark the commissioning of the first phase of the Aga Khan University (AKU) Sports Centre, a cricket match was held on December 13, 1998, between the Rector's XI, a team of faculty and students and the President's XI, consisting of staff and volunteers. The Chief Guest was Mr Zaheer Abbas, former Captain of the Pakistan cricket team.

AKU Sport Centre's Phase 1 facilities were completed on schedule, and include the cricket and football fields, tennis and volleyball courts and a jogging track. The Centre is expected to be fully operational in the year 2000, when it will offer various indoor, outdoor and water sports. Highlights of the Sports Centre include an air-conditioned gymnasium, Olympic length swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, weight training and aerobics rooms. One unique feature of the Centre will be its Patient Rehabilitation Programme. Designed to aid and facilitate the recovery of patients suffering from heart attacks, strokes, traffic accident disabilities and sports' injuries. It will be the first service of its kind in Pakistan.

Demonstrating a spirit of volunteer ism and giving, over 50,000 young people from 30 countries participated in the grassroots fund-raising campaign for the Rs.276 million Centre. A significant proportion of the contributions came from donors within Pakistan who rose more than Rs.36.8 million from the total fund-raising target of Rs.138 million. The balance of Rs.138 million was generously matched by His Highness the Aga Khan.

Designed in strict accordance with the highest international standards, the AKU Sports Centre's activities will complement academic programmes by enhancing the learning process and fostering a healthier environment. Although the Sports Centre will primarily be used by the University's students, faculty and staff, it will also serve as a venue for intercollegiate, national and international sports events. AKU Sports Centre will also provide much-needed facilities for women, who form the majority of the student body and the professional staff, and currently have little opportunity for sports and fitness activities.
The Sports Centre is a reflection of AKU's continuous commitment to excellence and broad outlook and will serve as a replicable model for other such facilities across the country."
